_doc: Delta ledger (tier-4 §5), both kinds. Append-only, one JSON object per line. Fields: asset, gap_id, kind (gap|opportunity), criterion, what, change, detector, owner, gate, state (OPEN|IN_PROGRESS|CLOSED|WITHDRAWN), ts. kind=gap: the shortfall against a requirement — `what` is written `measured: <figure, instrument, population> / required: <the gate's claim>` so the delta is a re-run, not a claim; gate = what it blocks (default: this asset's certification); CLOSED = the detector passed. kind=opportunity (tier-4 §9): the beyond — `what` = the distinction added or cost removed + expected delta; `change` = the proposal with cost and risk; `detector` = the measurement that proves it afterward; gate = NONE (an opportunity never blocks certification) and the row names the layer packet it feeds; OPEN=proposed, IN_PROGRESS=accepted and being built, CLOSED=realised and proven by its measurement, WITHDRAWN=rejected. A row with no detector/measurement is not registered — it is raised as a question. Rows without `kind` are read as kind=gap (pre-2026-09-26 rows).

what: measured: count_sql returns 741, of which 327 rows are produced by l0_yogas.py, l0_doshas.py and l0_dasha_systems.py / required: the cockpit credits an asset with its own rows
change: scope count_sql to this writer's rows, or declare brahma_ontology a multi-producer shared table in the registry
detector: per-class producer census; count_sql output equals the writer's declared row count

what: measured: asset_throughput.rows_written = 0 against 741 live rows, rows_per_second NULL, last_built_at 2026-09-04 / required: a build record carrying a real figure
change: instrument the seeder's run (rows, duration) into asset_throughput

what: measured: data plane 4.1 rule 1's detector is count(*) = count(DISTINCT canonical_id) ACROSS classes, which reports FAIL against data satisfying its own live constraint UNIQUE (entity_class, canonical_id) — 741 rows, 741 distinct composites, 0 duplicates / required: a detector that tests the authority's declared key
change: correct rule 1's detector to the composite key, or rule that the key must be simple — a sealed-document reopen either way
detector: re-run: the corrected detector passes on conformant data and fails on a seeded true duplicate
gate: layer packet W-L0-5 + sealed data plane reopen

what: measured: resolve_entity.ts returns two rows for the 11 ids present in two classes and applies a hard-coded ORDER BY (entity_class='varga') DESC preference — whose cited example, navamsa, exists in ONE class only, so the workaround addresses a condition not present in live data / required: consumers resolve on the declared composite key
change: make resolvers class-aware, or settle the key contract per opportunity O1
detector: join census: every consumer join returns exactly one row for all 741 identities

what: measured: no detector compares a row to its source_citation; 741/741 rows carry one / required: a source-correspondence detector that can fail
change: build the D1 detector (layer packet W-L0-3) and run it over this asset
detector: the detector reports a non-zero mismatch count it could also report as zero

what: measured: list_entities returns empty_reason stating entity_class='yoga' has no top-level class in brahma_ontology, against 233 live rows with exactly that class; dosha absent from VALID_ENTITY_CLASSES while matching 79 rows at runtime / required: a served surface's stated reason is true
change: delete the false UNBACKED_CLASSES branch; add yoga and dosha to the declared class vocabulary

what: measured: 79 of 79 dosha rows carry an empty synonyms array; the other 15 classes are complete / required: a non-empty closed alias set per entity
change: seed dosha alias sets through the writer
detector: per-class alias census: no_alias = 0 for all 16 classes

what: measured: normalisation is not declared at the authority; BPHS vs bphs is why 289 of 341 remedy source ids do not resolve / required: the normalisation rule declared once, at the authority, not at consumers
change: declare case and diacritic normalisation in the release; add the ambiguous-alias list

what: measured: no declared universe for 11 of 16 classes; the text class and the corpus both hold 15 members and differ by 3 in EACH direction (ontology-only: bhrigu_samhita, jaimini_sutram, lal_kitab_text; corpus-only: bhrigu_nandi_nadi, bphs_jaimini, nadi_navamsa_patel) / required: a declared universe per class, and the two sets reconciled
change: declare the universe per class; derive the text class from the corpus (opportunity O5)
detector: the 1.1 width census re-run: 0 in both directions for text; every class carries a declared universe

what: measured: 0 of 2 capability modules serving this asset declare a density_contract (0 of 46 layer-wide) / required: declared where the capability paginates or facets
change: declare density_contract on resolve_entity and list_entities
detector: grep census over the L0 capability directory

what: the distinction added: one resolvable identity for all 741 rows, removing the defect class behind G03, G04 and the layer instance's mis-stated finding permanently
change: three options: (a) keep the composite key and make every resolver and join class-aware — matches the writer's intent and the live constraint, cheapest; (b) make canonical_id globally unique and rename the 11 collisions — matches data plane 4.1 rule 1 as literally written; (c) keep the composite key and add a generated global_id (class:id) for single-token consumers. Cost: (a) touches every join on canonical_id; (b) touches 11 ids and their referrers; (c) additive. Risk: (b) breaks existing references silently if any are missed. NATIVE DECISION, not an asset fix.
detector: join census before and after: 11 ids return two rows today, 0 after
gate: NONE — feeds the layer packet W-L0-5

what: removes the provenance ambiguity behind G01: the identity authority currently has four writers
change: either split identity rows so each class has one producer, or declare brahma_ontology a multi-producer shared table with a scoped count_sql per asset. Cost: registry change plus possibly three writer changes. Risk: low — no data moves.
detector: per-class producer census; each class attributable to exactly one writer

what: makes 312 built rows reachable and declared (233 yoga + 79 dosha) — 58% -> 100% of rows reachable-and-declared
change: add yoga and dosha to VALID_ENTITY_CLASSES and remove the false UNBACKED_CLASSES branch. [TRANSFERS] — the requirement belongs to the retrieval plane; the measurement is here. Cost: small. Risk: none.

what: a real cost baseline where none exists: rows_written=0 today for a 741-row table
change: instrument seed_ontology to write rows and duration to asset_throughput. Cost: small. Risk: none. Output delta: none (same 414 rows seeded); input delta: none; build-cost delta: unmeasurable until it exists.
detector: the record carries a non-zero row count and a duration after one build, with output parity unchanged

what: fewer inputs and no drift: the text class duplicates what classical_text_chunks already knows, and the two have drifted by 3 in each direction
change: derive the text class from the corpus at seed time instead of declaring 15 members in a Python literal. Output delta: same or better (drift becomes impossible); input delta: fewer (one less hand-maintained list); build-cost delta: negligible.
detector: the 1.1 cross-check returns 0 in both directions by construction; output parity on the other 15 classes

what: one provable join instead of four assumed ones: bg_yogas, bg_doshas and bg_dasha_systems each seed identity rows here and keep their own catalogues
change: declare an identity contract between the ontology and the three catalogues — catalogue rows reference the ontology by its composite key. Beyond the layer: the same contract is what L2's fact ids resolve through. Cost: a contract plus three references. Risk: exposes existing mismatches, which is the point.
detector: ablation of seam A: break the identity reference and measure the served reading — today the seam cannot be broken because it is not declared
